mechanism: Oxybutynin's anticholinergic effects may potentiate medroxyprogesterone-related gastrointestinal effects and both agents can cause CNS depression; medroxyprogesterone is metabolized via CYP3A4 which oxybutynin weakly inhibits.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention) and CNS effects (drowsiness); no dose adjustment typically required but counsel on additive effects.
